overview.text: The Indian Rock Python is a large, non-venomous python of the Indian subcontinent - smaller and lighter-coloured than its relative the Burmese Python, but still one of the world's biggest snakes.

identification.text: Whitish or yellowish with tan to dark brown blotches; darker in hill forests, lighter on the Deccan Plateau.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Nearly all of the Indian subcontinent south of the Himalayas, including southern Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, south-eastern Pakistan and Bangladesh, and probably northern Myanmar.

habitat.text: Grassland, swamps, marshes, rocky foothills, woodland and forest.

behaviour.text: Slow and timid, and rarely tries to attack.

recognise.text: Huge python with brown blotches on a pale body.
